This test checks the EX-Gear's hover function.
rows.notes: 600-643 (Gary, Hilda): EX-Gear exam instructions at the Academy; Luis (om2 600-604) is the player's sparring opponent.

rows.en: So I'm your opponent today. Come on, show me your passion!
rows.notes: The MUF ref clip with this id is a different recording (a Miss Macross contest announcement); ignored.

rows.en: This test checks walking in the EX-Gear.
rows.notes: Transcript has ekusukia; read as EX-Gear (ekusugia).

rows.en: Hover mode lets you move fast, and climb and descend too. Master it and it'll help you out in all kinds of situations.
Let's see what you've got. Come at me!
rows.notes: The MUF ref clip with this id is a different recording (a Miss Macross contest announcement); ignored.

rows.en: Walking in an EX-Gear is nothing like walking on your own two feet. Get cocky and you'll get hurt.
It may be a bit hard to get into, but it's not that difficult. With the basics, practice beats theory.
Your skills aren't bad. But you're seriously lacking in passion.
Reach the goal, the room at the far end, and the test is over.
Same as last time: the test is to reach the goal.
My machine was restricted, sure, but to think I got shot down... I definitely felt your passion.
It's a straight path to the goal. You won't get lost. There's a time limit just in case, but no need to rush.
I've floated checkpoint markers too, so if you're confident, go for the bonus points.
Geez, skills like that won't make my soul tremble.
There are also checkpoint markers floating along the way.
rows.notes: Transcript has mada ('still'); read as mata ('also').

rows.en: If you're not used to high speed, you can lose track of where you are. Then it's fine to switch to Walk mode and land.
rows.notes: Mode names as in the corpus EX-Gear tutorial: Walk / Hover / Flight mode.

rows.en: Go around the markers before the goal and you get bonus points. Well, whether you go for them is your call.
Calm down, look around you, then head for the goal.
As you can see, this test course is a narrow passage.
This test checks the EX-Gear's flight maneuvers.
In Flight or Hover mode you could hit a wall and get hurt. Don't switch modes carelessly. Got it?
With this test, you'll have mastered all the EX-Gear's basic movement.
Moving on from the basics, this test applies them: we'll test shooting attacks.
As before, the test ends once you reach the goal.
It's called shooting, but this isn't the military. You won't be firing guns, so relax.
There are markers at the checkpoints. Go around them before the goal and you'll get bonus points.
You'll use paintballs. Just throw them and hit the targets. Well, it's more throwing than shooting.
You're done once you reach the goal in time. If you hit a wall and lose your bearings, land once and calm down.
Anyway, if you can't control your EX-Gear precisely, you won't even hit a target with a ball.
Flying straight shouldn't be that hard. Go after those markers aggressively.
The test: hit as many of the targets in the room as you can with balls.
The trick is using boost and brake well. If you're about to hit something, rolling away is one technique too. Remember that.
There are targets in the air too. Watch you don't miss them.
This test is about melee attacks.
Don't just throw balls around wildly. Don't forget to lock on properly before you throw.
The EX-Gear's a powered suit. Get used to using it like this too.
For this test, you'll be hauling containers.
The test is to take down training targets. One will do, but take down as many as you like within the time limit.
rows.notes: Transcript ends kamau ('mind'); read as kamawanai ('it's fine').

rows.en: It may be plain, simple work, but steady training like this is what leads to precise control. Remember that.
There's a volleyball machine set up with the targets. Balls fly out of it now and then. Dodge or block them, but deal with them.
rows.notes: Hilda (row 3190) says the machine was borrowed from the volleyball club.

rows.en: The test: bring the containers in each room back here. Set one down here and that delivery is done.
In melee you tend to focus on the enemy in front of you, but sometimes backing off to check around you matters. Remember that.
Some rooms have closed doors, but you can open them by working the switch.
This test takes place in the gravity control section.
Bring back at least one container to pass, but bring as many as you like within the time limit.
The room's at zero G, with footage of space projected. Well? Feels like you're really out in space, huh?
Every container you bring back adds bonus points.
Reach the goal and this test is over.
This test has no particularly tricky rules.
Targets are floating as markers to the goal. Follow them and you'll get there.
The point is to see how well you each can handle an EX-Gear.
There are a few checkpoint markers again. If you're confident, go around them before the goal.
The test is to reach the goal beyond the hill before time runs out.
Space has no up or down, so everyone's thrown at first.
rows.notes: Transcript writes kankaku as 'interval'; read as kankaku 'sense (of up and down)'.

rows.en: Take whatever route you like. Fly or walk, it doesn't matter.
Normally, you'd never head out into space without any guidance in the first place.
There are checkpoint markers floating here and there.
